beats.say: Hello! The archive department keeps ten years of documents. Today you learn how to keep their copies the right way.
Ransomware encrypts more than the computer. It also locks the flash drive plugged into it and the network folder.

body.text: Connected drives and the network folder are locked too.

beats.say: The rule: three copies, two kinds of media, one somewhere else. At least one must be fully off the network.

visual.label: 3 copies, 2 kinds of media, 1 copy off-site

beats.say: And remember: an untested copy can turn out empty when you need it. Test a restore from time to time.

question.prompt: A ransom note is on the screen. Which copy most likely survived?

options.label: The flash drive left plugged into the computer
options.feedback: A connected drive is like part of the computer. Ransomware encrypts it too.

options.label: The cloud folder that syncs automatically
options.feedback: Syncing copies the encrypted files to the cloud too. Older versions sometimes remain, but you cannot count on it.

options.label: The department's network folder
options.feedback: If the computer can reach the network folder, so can the ransomware.

options.label: The disk unplugged on Friday and locked in the safe
options.feedback: Correct. A disk cut off from the computer and the network stays out of reach during an attack.

scenes.explain: The copy that survives an attack is the one off the network. That is why one copy is always unplugged and kept apart.

scenes.title: Archive department
scenes.intro: You work in the archive department. From Friday evening to Monday, make the right call in every window.

body.text: ARXIV-DISK: ten years of documents, 212 GB. You can remove the disk now.

actions.label: Eject disk
actions.feedback: Correct. An ejected disk cannot be encrypted in the next attack.

actions.label: Keep connected
actions.feedback: A connected disk can be encrypted along with the computer. Eject it as soon as the backup ends.

body.text: Restore one folder from the latest copy as a test?

actions.label: Test restore
actions.feedback: Well done. Only a copy that opens is a real copy.

actions.label: Skip
actions.feedback: The copy may be broken, and you would find out at the worst moment. Test restores regularly.

title.text: Upload the folder to your personal account?

actions.label: Upload
actions.feedback: Work documents belong only where your office has approved. A personal cloud does not protect the copy and can leak the data.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: Correct. If an extra copy is needed, technical support creates it in an approved place.

steps.label: Monday, 09:05

body.text: The network folder and connected drives are locked. Pay within 72 hours for the key.

steps.say: On Monday morning, this message is on the screen.

actions.label: Unplug cable, turn off Wi-Fi
actions.feedback: Correct. Cut it off from the network without shutting it down, and call technical support right away.

actions.label: Pay
actions.feedback: Paying does not guarantee the files come back. Recovery will come from the copy you kept apart.

body.text: The department folder was synced to the cloud.

actions.label: Tell technical support
actions.feedback: Correct, syncing copied the encrypted files too. A specialist will restore the older versions.

actions.label: Restore from the cloud myself
actions.feedback: Files restored onto an infected computer can be encrypted again. Specialists restore on a clean computer.

title.text: Bring the disk from the safe

body.text: Do not plug ARXIV-DISK in anywhere. We will restore together on a clean computer.

actions.label: I hand the disk to the specialist
actions.feedback: Well done. The restore will happen on a cleaned computer, under a specialist's control.

actions.label: I plug the disk into this computer myself
actions.feedback: The last copy can get encrypted on an infected computer. Give the disk only to the specialist.

scenes.prompt: Match each part of the rule with its meaning.

pairs.right: The original file and two backups
For example, an external disk and an approved cloud
In another building and off the network
Checking regularly that the copy opens

scenes.explain: With three copies, two media and one copy off-site, if one is lost another remains. A restore test proves the copy works.

question.prompt: Where do you keep important work documents?

options.label: In my office's approved folder
options.feedback: Correct. Technical support makes and checks the copies there.

options.label: On the desktop, and I copy them to my own flash drive in the evening
options.feedback: A personal flash drive can get lost or infected. Nobody checks a copy like that.

options.label: In my personal cloud account, it is handy
options.feedback: In a personal account, a work document leaves your office's control. That is also a data leak.

scenes.explain: Technical support protects and restores the copy of a file kept in an approved place. A work file kept elsewhere is neither protected nor restored.

points: Three copies, two media, one off-site.
Keep at least one copy off the network.
